question: Can textbook proof-tree deletion or any-win return be counted as new free capability in the current exact-policy route?
existing_baseline: Public mainline already keeps qualifying completed root wins after later abort and optionally stops at any WIN; it preserves source/completed-depth metadata.

witness_memory.paper: Pages5-6/30 delete proved/disproved subtrees to reduce stored nodes while retaining proof/disproof truth summaries.
witness_memory.current_consumer: Current certificate(node) recursively needs concrete selected OR edge and all AND edges, and SessionStrategyCursor later follows that concrete tree.
witness_memory.deduction: Deleting the stored witness merely because pn==0 is not a drop-in memory optimization for this independently verified/cursor route. A value summary alone cannot regenerate full typed legal-defense evidence.
witness_memory.alternatives: Retaining a compact witness or regenerating it are distinct space/time choices with construction/verification cost; neither was implemented or measured. Do not infer depth-first memory savings for the retained-tree prototype.

rank_units.certificate_rank: Upper bound on worst-case remaining strategy edges in the returned witness, not shortest mate over all strategies.
rank_units.peak_depth: Maximum depth inspected by PN, not a complete uniform search layer.
rank_units.completed_depth: Uniform iteration depth retained by alpha-beta, with q-policy provenance separate.
rank_units.consequence: No ratio between these fields is a depth or speed advantage. Multiple winning actions have equal WDL even if witness lengths differ.

exploration_not_gate: The unknown online trigger rate and witness overhead motivate one cheap bounded matched test, not mandatory full-game proof/calibration before exploratory work. Existing user authorization remains; no new approval queue follows.
